memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Appoint judges and officials for each of your tribes in every town the Lord your God is giving you, and they shall judge the people fairly. Do not pervert justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the innocent. - Deut 16:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God now turns from feasts to fairness. He commands the appointing of judges who will judge the people justly, without twisting the truth, without favouring some over others, and without taking bribes. God cares deeply about justice, because justice reflects His own character.

Look at how sharply God speaks about bribes, they blind the wise and twist the words of the innocent. Corruption does not just harm one case; it corrodes a whole society and crushes the vulnerable who cannot pay. God wanted His people to be different, a community where the poor could expect fair treatment as surely as the powerful.

This matters for us too. Our God is perfectly just. He never takes bribes, never shows favouritism, and always judges rightly (Rom 2:11). Because He is like this, His people are called to reflect His fairness in how we treat others, in our workplaces, our families, and our dealings with the weak. We are not to flatter the rich and ignore the poor (Jas 2:1-4). And how comforting to know that the final Judge of all cannot be bought or fooled. In a world full of crooked scales, we can rest in the perfect justice of God. Where might God be calling you to act fairly and refuse favouritism?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to show favouritism?
2. How does God's perfect justice comfort and challenge you?
3. Who around you needs to be treated more fairly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are perfectly just and never partial. Make me fair and honest, reflecting Your justice to those around me. Amen.
